transcript.text: I'm at 72 and west end. I have 25 minutes. Im looking for something related to music history

A rare master tape of a legendary 1950s rock-and-roll recording session has gone missing from an Upper West Side vault, and you're on the trail to recover it. This quick 1-stop adventure takes about 11 minutes total.

To reach your first stop at the historic Pythian Temple:
1. Walk southeast on West 72nd Street.
2. Turn right onto Broadway and keep left to stay on Broadway as you head toward West 70th Street.

Let me know when you've arrived outside 135 West 70th Street!

Welcome to the Pythian Temple at 135 West 70th Street. 

Back when Decca Records ran a studio here on the third floor [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pythian_Temple_(New_York_City)), legendary tracks were cut in that auditorium—including Bill Haley recording "Rock Around the Clock" and Buddy Holly's famous 1958 string sessions [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pythian_Temple_(New_York_City)).

Look up at the building's unique neo-Babylonian facade and describe one architectural detail or feature you notice.
Assyrian type heads on the colimns

Spot on! Those striking neo-Babylonian and Assyrian-inspired details make this building completely unique on the Upper West Side.

Your radio crackles to life as Agent Vance checks in: *"Great eye. That confirms you're at the right spot. We intercepted a digital dispatch fragment mentioning a lost recording session from 1958 right here at the Pythian [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pythian_Temple_(New_York_City))."*

***

### Case File: The Missing Master Tape

* **Stops Visited:** Pythian Temple (135 West 70th Street)
* **Real Facts Learned:** 
  - Built in 1927 by architect Thomas W. Lamb in an Exotic / neo-Babylonian style, the Pythian Temple originally served as a meeting place for New York City's Pythian lodges [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pythian_Temple_(New_York_City)).
  - In the 1940s, Decca Records converted its large third-floor auditorium into a legendary recording studio [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pythian_Temple_(New_York_City)).
  - Iconic tracks recorded here include Bill Haley and His Comets' "Rock Around the Clock" (1954) and Buddy Holly's final 1958 "String Sessions" [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pythian_Temple_(New_York_City)).
* **Your Observation:** You spotted the striking neo-Babylonian heads framing the facade.
* **Solution:** The missing master tape was safely recovered from the old Pythian Temple recording vault, preserving rock-and-roll history!
